entries.title: First Results from JACKS: A VLA Ammonia View of Gas Heating and Star-forming Cores in the Central Molecular Zone
entries.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) combines warm molecular gas, strong turbulence, and a star-formation rate below that expected from its dense-gas reservoir. The JVLA Ammonia C-configuration K-band Survey (JACKS) is designed to connect these environmental conditions to the thermal and kinematic structure of compact, potentially star-forming gas. JACKS follows the footprint of the ALMA Central Molecular Zone Exploration Survey (ACES) with 31 Very Large Array mosaic fields. Its K-band setup covers the metastable NH$_3$ $(1,1)$--$(5,5)$ inversion transitions, five non-metastable NH$_3$ lines, the 22-GHz H$_2$O maser transition, H64$α$ and H66$α$, and broad continuum windows. The nominal resolutions are approximately $1.5''$ ($0.06$ pc at the Galactic Centre) and $0.4$ km s$^{-1}$ for the NH$_3$ lines. We present preliminary imaging products that demonstrate water-maser self-calibration, compact and extended continuum emission, filamentary NH$_3$ structure, and complex compact sources with multiple velocity components. Tests that combine JACKS with the SWAG and HOPS ammonia surveys recover progressively larger angular scales. These early products establish the survey's ability to connect core-scale gas heating and kinematics to the cloud-scale CMZ environment; quantitative temperature, opacity, and core-population measurements will follow from the uniformly reduced data set.

entries.title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
entries.abstract: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. This expanded sample provides an unprecedented opportunity to test the predictions of cosmological simulations and discriminate between competing physical prescriptions.

entries.title: Constraining the timescale of activity in Mrk 1018
entries.abstract: We present analysis of an extended emission line region projected 3.77 kpc from the nucleus of the canonical changing-look AGN Mrk~1018, found in MUSE integral-field observations from the Close AGN Reference Survey. Emission-line ratios show that the region exhibits AGN ionisation but has a very low velocity dispersion, $77 \pm 1$ kms$^{-1}$, ruling out an ionised outflow. The lower limit on the light travel time is $12{,}300 \pm 2{,}300$ yr, implying that the nucleus has therefore been active for at least this long. This is much longer than the duration of either observed changing-look transition, which occurred over several years. This implies that Mrk 1018's multi-year variations are occurring within a longer term active phase.

entries.title: Violent relaxation in hierarchical stellar systems: pathways toward massive black hole formation in the early Universe
entries.abstract: Massive stellar systems have been detected in the high-redshift Universe via the James Webb Space Telescope using gravitational lensing techniques. Such stellar systems may evolve on short dynamical timescales, despite a formally large 2-body relaxation time. If the stellar system consists of a large number of gravitationally bound clusters, a 2-body relaxation time can be defined for the star clusters in analogy to the 2-body relaxation time for stars, implying a faster evolution determined by the number of stars per cluster. At their formation, clusters will go through a process of "cold collapse" as part of their early, non-collisional, evolution. This phase enhances the mass segregation between the more massive and less massive population of stars. We derive a criteria based on the mass of the two components that determines under which conditions the massive component may even decouple from the cluster itself. Mergers of clusters and multiple mergers on average tend to produce systems with larger cluster radii. For the formation of massive black holes via dense stellar systems, the most promising pathway consists in the cold collapse of a dense massive cluster, after few mergers (or possibly none). In such a cluster with a sufficient number of massive stars, the massive population of stars will dynamically decouple in the central region and go through core collapse, leading to the formation of a central massive object. In the case of multiple mergers, massive but more spatially extended stellar systems will form.

entries.title: The Pristine survey XXXI. A stream offset from the Stream: very metal-poor stellar debris trailing 100$^{\circ}$ from the LMC-SMC system
entries.abstract: Context: The stellar counterpart to the $200^\circ$-long HI Stream from the Clouds probes their tidally stripped stellar populations and constrains their interaction history and structure before infall into the Milky Way. Aims: We investigate the chemodynamics and possible origin of very metal-poor (VMP; [Fe/H] $<-2$) stars in the stellar Stream, targeting distant red giants selected from the Pristine--Gaia synthetic metallicity catalogue. Methods: We obtained high-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidate members, deriving radial velocities and metallicities. We combine these data with literature red giant members and assess their association with the Clouds using orbital integrations in a time-dependent Milky Way--LMC potential. We also compare their distribution with collisionless test particles initially placed in a diffuse LMC stellar halo. Results: We identify 12 high-confidence members based on energy and angular momentum: one intermediate metal-poor star ([Fe/H] $\sim-1.6$), ten VMP stars, and one extremely metal-poor (EMP) star ([Fe/H] $<-3$). The new VMP stars trace over $100^\circ$ of the trailing Stream, follow the Clouds' kinematics, and lie $\sim20^\circ$ from both the HI Stream and previously known, more metal-rich debris, suggesting a metallicity-dependent spatial distribution. Combined with the literature, they approximately double the known red giant sample and extend its metallicity range from [Fe/H] $\sim-0.5$ to $-4.3$. Orbital integrations support an association with the Clouds, while test particles reproduce the debris' broad spatial distribution. Conclusions: VMP and EMP stars contribute to the Clouds' tidal debris. They may originate in the extended stellar halos of the LMC or SMC, or in disrupted satellites. Their spatial and kinematic properties can constrain future simulations of the Milky Way--LMC--SMC interaction.

entries.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
entries.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

entries.title: The Influence of the Inclination of the Accretion Disk in Black Hole X-Ray Binaries on the Energy Spectrum Characteristics
entries.abstract: During the ascending and descending phases of some black hole X-ray binaries(BH XRBs), it was found that the X-ray Eddington ratio ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $) and the photon spectral index $Γ$ had an anticorrelation when the X-ray Eddington ratio was less than a specific value, and a positive correlation when it was greater than that value. Moreover, the cross points of the anticorrelation and positive correlation are different for different BH XRBs ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $ of cross point is between $ 0.1 \% $ and $ 10\% $). The reason why the cross points are different for different BH XRBs were still uncertain. So we processed the light curve and energy spectrum of 15 outbursts of eight BH XRBs during their descending phases. We found that for the same BH XRB, the values of the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point are basically consistent for different outburst times. However, for different BH XRBs, there is a positive linear correlation between the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point and the cosine of the accretion disk inclination. Therefore, We think that the geometric effect of the inclination has a significant impact on the evolution of the energy spectrum of the BH XRBs.

entries.title: A Large-Sample Study of Interstellar Reddening in Galactic Star Clusters
entries.abstract: The interstellar reddening (extinction or absorption) is caused mainly by the dust grains of different sizes and compounds. All astrophysical observations are somehow affected by this effect, depending on the wavelength and location of the observed object. Different methods and techniques have been developed over the last nearly one hundred years to determine the reddening and to map the solar neighbourhood. The members of open clusters are a consistent population of stars formed together with a homogeneous metallicity. Therefore, the reddening can be estimated in a statistical way, avoiding all problems of single stars and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, for example. Other than for most available works, we can also use more massive upper main-sequence stars for the analysis. We used classical colour-colour diagrams (also known as the Q-method) for (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G) to determine consistent mean reddening values and their errors. The corresponding standard lines for the fitting are independent of the age and metallicity. We determined colour excesses for 5377 Galactic open clusters covering Galactocentric distances from two to twenty kpc, respectively. The derived values were checked with existing dust and extinction maps. In general, we found good agreement. The solar neighbourhood of +-1500 pc shows a very patchy structure of the dust composition. Our results lay the foundations for constructing a new map of the reddening (dust) distribution and estimating clusters' metallicities by isochrone fitting, keeping the distances and reddening values fixed.

entries.title: Discovery of the redback pulsar PSR J2053+6905 and multi-epoch optical observations of the system
entries.abstract: Using the Green Bank Telescope, we discovered the 1.68-ms binary pulsar PSR J2053+6905. The discovery resulted from a targeted search for radio pulsations from a redback candidate, previously identified through optical and X-ray observations and spatially coincident with the $γ$-ray source 4FGL J2054.2+6904. We report the first results from the pulsar timing, including the spin period, dispersion measure, precisely measured Keplerian binary parameters, and the pulsar mass function. We also found potential evidence of scintillation and long radio eclipses. To constrain the system parameters, we performed multi-epoch time-series photometric observations using the 2.1-m telescope at the Observatorio Astronómico Nacional on the Sierra San Pedro Mártir (Mexico) and the 1.5-m telescope of the Maidanak Astronomical Observatory (Uzbekistan), complemented by time-series optical spectroscopy with the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias. The optical light curves revealed a pronounced asymmetry, as well as significant long-term variations. From the spectra, we derived a radial velocity curve semi-amplitude $K = 337(4)$ km s$^{-1}$. Combining it with the pulsar mass function, we constrained the ratio of pulsar and companion masses to $M_{\rm p}/M_{\rm c} = 7.05(8)$. By fitting the stable segments of the light curves with a symmetric direct heating model, we derived constraints on the component masses ($M_{\rm p} \approx 2.1\ {\rm M}_\odot$ and $M_{\rm c} \approx 0.3\ {\rm M}_\odot$), the Roche lobe filling factor, and the companion's day- and night-side temperatures. The long-term evolution of the light curve profiles is likely driven by the dissipation or migration of a cold stellar spot.

entries.title: Thorium and Europium production in the early Galaxy: Implications for nucleocosmochronology
entries.abstract: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology, with the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio providing a promising chronometer. We assess the reliability of log(Th/Eu) as an age indicator by testing whether thorium and europium were co-produced in a constant ratio in metal-poor stars, and evaluate the uncertainties affecting stellar ages. We present new Th and Eu abundance measurements for eight TITANS reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. Combining these measurements with homogeneous literature samples, we investigate the behaviour of log(Th/Eu) as a function of metallicity. We derive ages adopting a theoretical initial r-process production ratio and assess the effects of observational uncertainties and sample statistics. At low metallicity, the observed Th/Eu ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity after excluding stars with anomalous actinide abundances, supporting broadly uniform Th and Eu co-production in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are consistent with expectations for an old, metal-poor halo population, although individual uncertainties remain substantial. Higher spectral resolution is needed to improve Th measurements, while combining stars in coeval populations can provide additional statistical gains. Nucleocosmochronology offers an independent approach to dating the oldest stellar populations. Homogeneous samples of coeval stars, particularly in globular clusters, observed with future high-resolution multi-object spectrographs could provide stronger constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

entries.title: FALCON (FERMI-ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN): Cross-matching ALMA Calibrators with Fermi-LAT Blazars
entries.abstract: Blazars are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets closely aligned with our line of sight, producing Doppler-boosted emission from radio to gamma rays. Millimeter emission near the synchrotron self-absorption turnover probes compact regions at the jet base, yet large statistical studies in this regime remain limited. We construct the FALCON (FERMI--ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN) catalogue, a millimeter-selected blazar sample by cross-matching the ALMA Calibrator Source Catalogue with the Third Data Release of the Fourth LAT AGN Catalog (4LAC-DR3). After removing duplicates, we obtain 949 unique gamma-ray-associated sources, corresponding to approximately 25 % of the 4LAC-DR3 blazar population. For the subset with available redshift measurements, we compute millimeter and gamma-ray luminosities and find a strong, statistically significant correlation that remains robust after accounting for redshift effects. Fermi-detected blazars exhibit systematically flatter millimeter spectral indices than gamma-ray non-detected ALMA calibrators, while the redshift-controlled luminosity correlation becomes progressively weaker from high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacs toward flat-spectrum radio quasars. These results indicate an intrinsic connection between millimeter and gamma-ray emission, consistent with a common origin in relativistic jets governed by Doppler boosting and time-averaged jet power.

entries.title: Multi-epoch monitoring of the faint northern component in 3C 84 during 2016-2021
entries.abstract: We present the results of multi-epoch very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations of the sub-parsec-scale northern jet component of 3C 84 (known as the N1 component) at 7 mm from 2016 to 2021. The peak position of the N1 component exhibits positional variations of approximately 0.2 mas at a distance of about 2.5 mas from the central radio core (C1) throughout the observation period. Although a linear fit yields a small proper motion of $μ_{\rm{Dec}}=0.054\pm0.019~\rm{mas}~\rm{yr}^{-1}$, corresponding to an apparent velocity of $β_{\rm{app}}=0.062\pm0.021$, this displacement is comparable to the observed positional scatter, and the hypothesis that N1 exhibits systematic motion is not statistically supported. In contrast, the peak flux density varies by approximately a factor of two on timescales of several months. We propose two possible explanations for the observed behavior of N1. One is that N1 is the counterpart of the southern hotspot C3, but its motion has been halted by a collision with a compact and dense cloud along its path; in this case, the flux variability may be caused by changes in the free-free absorption opacity of the non-uniform cloud. The other possibility is that N1 is part of the northern jet that is heavily obscured by foreground free-free absorption and is observed through a gap in the absorbing medium; in this case, the variability may reflect intrinsic changes in the jet and its interaction with a non-uniform ambient medium. These results provide new constraints on the physical origin of N1 and on the circumnuclear environment of 3C 84.

entries.title: Cepheid Metallicity in the Leavitt Law (C-MetaLL) survey: X First spectroscopic characterization of Galactic Type II Cepheids and calibration of the Period-Wesenheit-Metallicity relations
entries.abstract: Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are Population II pulsating stars that serve as distance indicators through their period--luminosity relation. Along with RR Lyrae stars and the tip of the red giant branch, they offer an independent route to the Hubble constant, helping assess systematic uncertainties in its determination. We aim to investigate the impact of chemical composition on T2Cs' period--luminosity relations by building a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of Galactic T2Cs with iron and oxygen abundances. We observed 80 Galactic T2Cs with UVES at the ESO Very Large Telescope. For 74 stars, we derived stellar parameters and iron and oxygen abundances through a self-consistent spectroscopic analysis based on equivalent widths of absorption lines. This sample nearly doubles the number of T2Cs with spectroscopic metallicity measurements available in the literature. We used these abundances to test theoretical predictions for the instability strip and, together with $Gaia$ parallaxes, to derive Period--Wesenheit--metallicity (PWZ) relations. In agreement with theoretical predictions, the metallicity coefficient ($γ$) is small and statistically consistent with zero in all relations, ranging from approximately $-0.02$ to $+0.17$ mag dex$^{-1}$. We also estimated distances to 22 Galactic Globular Clusters hosting T2Cs, finding agreement within uncertainties with independent literature estimates. Our results show that metallicity has, at most, a minor impact on T2Cs' pulsation properties and distance scale, supporting their reliability as Population II distance indicators.

entries.title: Multi-layer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
entries.abstract: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry. Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations. The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3°\pm0.8°$ in the northwest to $162.2°\pm0.6°$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~μ\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures. Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

entries.title: Survey of Surveys Data Release 3. Homogenised stellar parameters across nine spectroscopic surveys
entries.abstract: Large spectroscopic surveys have measured atmospheric parameters for millions of Milky Way stars, but differences in instruments, wavelength ranges, analysis methods, and assumptions introduce survey-dependent systematics that complicate their joint use. We aim to place effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity estimates from major spectroscopic surveys onto a common, externally validated scale, and to provide a homogenised catalogue for large-scale Galactic studies. We construct the calibration hierarchically. We first define an internal reference scale from the best-populated and best-overlapped surveys (APOGEE, GALAH, and LAMOST LRS), and model survey-to-reference corrections and their uncertainties with machine-learning regression. The scale is then extended to LAMOST MRS, Gaia RVS, RAVE, DESI, Gaia-ESO, and SEGUE, and anchored to high-quality measurements from the PASTEL database. The calibration reduces survey-to-survey offsets and improves consistency in independent overlap samples: independent calibration of GALAH and LAMOST LRS temperatures onto the APOGEE scale reduces their median offset from 44.5 K to 6.2 K. The final catalogue contains about 10.13 million stars, including 6.10 million in the recommended high-quality subset and 3.69 million in the metallicity-optimised subset. For the high-quality subset, Gaia benchmark stars give median residuals of 30 K in $T_{\rm eff}$, 0.03 dex in $\log g$, and $-0.02$ dex in [Fe/H]. The [Fe/H]-optimised subset gives median residuals of 0.003 dex against Gaia benchmark stars, 0.05 dex for globular clusters, and $-0.02$ dex for open clusters. As an example application, we confirm the presence of metal-poor stars on thin-disc-like orbits, including stars with [Fe/H] $< -2$, showing that the catalogue can be used to study rare Galactic populations on a consistent multi-survey scale.

entries.title: Mass loss in AF supergiants: At the verge of the Eddington limit and still with weak line-driven winds
entries.abstract: We study global atmosphere models of AF supergiants. In agreement with previous studies, we found super-Eddington layers in the photospheres of these stars, which lead to density inversions. Our tests showed that the super-Eddington layers are caused by hydrogen ionization. The analysis of radial perturbations has not revealed any instability of such layers, but we show that super-Eddington layers in an optically thick environment are prone to instabilities due to nonradial perturbations. We predict the wind parameters of AF supergiants from our global wind code with a comoving-frame radiative force. Despite the existence of density inversions, the predicted mass-loss rates are significantly lower than those estimated from observations. Theoretical values approach the observational estimates only for the most luminous supergiants, which are close to the Eddington limit due to light scattering on free electrons. Part of the discrepancy between the mass-loss rates could be attributed to the influence of the clumping on the observational properties. Low mass-loss rates imply that the winds of AF supergiants may be strongly influenced by the magnetic fields, suggesting an explanation for the observed spectral variability of these stars.

analysis.reason: Directly relevant to magnetar-powered transients, this work quantifies crustal baryon ejection, neutrino effects, and nucleosynthesis in giant flares. Its limits on deep-crust escape provide useful tests of heavy-element production and flare-outflow models, even though the assumed geometry restricts direct application.
analysis.result: For flare-layer pressures labelled by $B=10^{15}$–$10^{16.5}\,\mathrm{G}$, with $P_{\rm GF}\simeq B^2/(8\pi)$, the simulations eject $M_{\rm ej}=1.2\times10^{-10}$–$4.8\times10^{-8}M_\odot$. Here $B$ labels the imposed pressure, not an evolved magnetic field. Over B15.0–B16.0, $M_{\rm ej}\propto P_{\rm GF}^{1.1}$, flattening to an exponent of approximately $0.4$ at higher pressure; neutrinos reduce the strongest model's ejecta mass by 46%. Mass-weighted terminal speeds are $0.44$–$0.52c$, while $E_{\rm kin}/E_{\rm fb}=6.8\times10^{-4}$–$1.5\times10^{-3}$. Approximately 90% of the ejecta becomes $\alpha$ particles and 7%–10% remains free neutrons: high entropy and rapid expansion suppress seed formation. The maximum mass of nuclei with $A\ge90$ is $3.5\times10^{-11}M_\odot$, and these heavy-element yields are probably upper limits, uncertain by up to a factor of two for $A\ge90$ and more for lanthanides and actinides. Deep crust invoked by the compared analytic model does not escape in these simulations.
analysis.reading_entry: VI Discussion and conclusions; then IV.2 Properties of the ejecta, IV.5 Nucleosynthesis, and V.3 Nucleosynthesis.
analysis.problem: Can a giant-flare-heated surface layer drive a shock into a neutron-star crust and eject enough deep, neutron-rich material to support substantial r-process nucleosynthesis? The study also investigates how neutrino cooling and weak interactions modify the escaping mass and electron fraction $Y_e$, and whether crustal shock ejection can explain inferred giant-flare outflows.
analysis.method: Spherically symmetric AthenaK general-relativistic neutrino-radiation hydrodynamics on a fixed TOV spacetime, using a nuclear EOS, energy-integrated two-moment M1 neutrino transport, and matched calculations without neutrinos. The initial star has $M_{\rm NS}=1.40M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm NS}=13.24\,\mathrm{km}$. analysis.result: The integrated 19–64 keV polarization is $\mathrm{PD}=5.0^{+2.7}_{-3.0}\%$ with $\mathrm{PA}=(-28\pm17)^\circ$. On July 12–13, $\mathrm{PD}=(16.8\pm4.9)\%$, with PA displaced by approximately $24^\circ$ from the radio jet. This is an approximately $3.4\sigma$ polarization detection, not a comparably significant detection of variability: its PD exceeds the combined remaining observations by only approximately $1.8\sigma$, and the trial-corrected joint Stokes probability is 1.7%. The relativistic reflection fraction increases from $R_f=0.11\pm0.02$ in S3 to $0.25^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$ in S4; fixing the electron temperature still yields $R_f=0.22\pm0.03$, more than $3\sigma$ above S3. analysis.problem: Does hard-X-ray polarization remain stable while Cyg X-1 is in a steady hard state, and can simultaneous reflection changes distinguish a changing inner corona from scattering by the companion or its wind?
analysis.method: Combine daily XL-Calibur 19–64 keV Bayesian polarization measurements with NICER, NuSTAR and Swift-BAT spectroscopy. Test variability using normalized Stokes parameters: a constant fit gives $\chi^2=22$ for 14 degrees of freedom. Jointly fit 1–195 keV spectra with MBPO × TBABS × (DISKBB + NTHCOMP + RELXILLCP + XILLVERCP), including cross-calibration $M(E)=N(E/E_{\rm br})^{\Delta\Gamma}$. Use MCMC to obtain 90% spectral intervals and compare reflection fractions between intervals. Systematic checks include background and modulation-curve fits; their fitting errors are explicitly not treated as true polarization measurement uncertainties.
limits: Appendix modulation-fit errors are fitting errors only, not true measurement errors, and cannot independently establish polarization significance or variability.

analysis.reason: The fading of a persistently active black-hole microquasar provides useful constraints on accretion–jet coupling, obscuration, and residual ejecta emission. It is relevant to compact-object high-energy observations and relativistic jets, although the intrinsic X-ray luminosity and the origin of the remaining radio emission remain uncertain.
analysis.result: The radio decline supports intrinsic fading of the central engine rather than obscuration alone, and the authors argue that the outburst beginning in 1992 has probably ended. July 2026 stacked measurements give $S_{1.28\,\mathrm{GHz}}=150\pm34\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$ and $S_{2.62\,\mathrm{GHz}}=93\pm11\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$, corresponding to $L_{\rm R}=(2.0\pm0.5)\times10^{28}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $d=9.4\,\mathrm{kpc}$. With $S_\nu\propto\nu^\alpha$, the spectrum has $\alpha=-0.67\pm0.36\,\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.20\,\mathrm{(sys)}$, and no variability is detected over six days. The FXT constraint is $L_{\rm X}\lesssim8.6\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, but unknown local absorption prevents treating this as a secure intrinsic luminosity limit. Comparison-sample fits, excluding GRS 1915+105, give $L_{\rm X}\propto P_{\rm orb}^{1.19^{+0.34}_{-0.29}}$ and $L_{\rm R}\propto P_{\rm orb}^{1.35^{+0.41}_{-0.27}}$, with $p=0.007$ and $0.04$, respectively. The source is compatible with these quiescent luminosity–period relations.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2 The interplay between obscuration and intrinsic fading
analysis.problem: Does the radio fading mark the end of the decades-long outburst and entry into quiescence, or merely a temporary reduction in activity? Compton-thick obscuration makes X-ray nondetections ambiguous, while the faint steep-spectrum radio emission could arise from residual optically thin ejecta, a compact jet, or a mixture of components.
analysis.method: The study combines long-term MeerKAT and AMI-LA monitoring, approximately eight hours of July 2026 MeerKAT observations in each of the L and S bands, and three Einstein Probe/FXT observations. Radio fluxes are measured with restoring-beam-constrained Gaussian fits plus a constant background; detections require amplitudes above $3\sigma$. Radio luminosities use $L_{\rm R}=4\pi d^2\nu S_\nu$. FXT upper limits are estimated through count-rate conversion and Cash-statistic spectral fitting, adopting an absorbed power law with $N_{\rm H}=1.4\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ and photon index $\Gamma=1.5$. The radio/X-ray comparison uses $\log(L_{\rm R}/L_{{\rm R},0})=\xi+\beta\log(L_{\rm X}/L_{{\rm X},0})$, with comparison slope $\beta=0.57\pm0.03$. Censored Kendall tests and Tobit fits assess the period relations using $\log_{10}L=a+b\log_{10}[P_{\rm orb}/(10\,\mathrm{hr})]$.
assumptions: The comparison retains published X-ray energy bands; the estimated bandpass mismatch of at most approximately a factor of two assumes $\Gamma\approx2$.
limits: Unknown intrinsic absorption can make the FXT luminosity constraint underestimate the intrinsic X-ray luminosity; X-ray nondetections alone cannot distinguish obscuration from fading.
The radio luminosity–period fit contains only five detections and twelve upper limits, leaving its normalization relatively uncertain.
The comparison sample uses heterogeneous published X-ray energy bands, introducing up to an approximately factor-of-two mismatch for $\Gamma\approx2$.

analysis.reason: This is a useful methodological contribution to neutron-star matter inference from gravitational waves, with indirect relevance to compact-object research rather than a direct application to high-energy transient emission. Its treatment of prior-induced bias and unreliable posterior reweighting is transferable to other weakly constrained inference problems.
analysis.result: In simulated binary-neutron-star signals, the Goldilocks prior reduces tidal-inference biases relative to the tested uniform and existing EoS-informed priors, including signals outside the adopted EoS ensemble. For $m_1=m_2=1.4\,M_\odot$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}_{\rm inj}=25$, below the ensemble minimum of 67.4, its posterior peaks recover the injected value at network SNRs of 10, 15, and 30. For an asymmetric system with $q=0.6$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}_{\rm inj}=25$, it yields $q=0.600\,[0.596,0.605]$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}=27.1\,[10.0,46.8]$ at SNR 100, with 90% credible intervals. Improvement is not universal: for the $1.8+1.6\,M_\odot$ injection with $\tilde{\Lambda}_{\rm inj}=10$, all three full Bayesian analyses still give approximately $\tilde{\Lambda}=21$ at SNR 100 because of mass-ratio boundary effects. An accompanying physical explanation of induced tidal priors uses $k_2\propto m^{-\alpha}$ and approximately constant radius, giving $\Lambda\propto m^{-5-\alpha}$.
analysis.problem: Weakly measured tidal parameters can inherit substantial structure from supposedly uninformative priors, while strict EoS-based priors can exclude physically relevant signals outside their ensemble. Finite posterior samples also prevent importance reweighting from reliably repairing regions that were poorly sampled initially. The central problem is to retain physical mass–tidal correlations without imposing excessively restrictive prior support.
analysis.method: Construct a four-dimensional conditional prior in $(\mathcal{M}_c,q,\tilde{\Lambda},\delta\tilde{\Lambda})$ from 105000 EoSs, drawing 1000 mass pairs per EoS and retaining models with $m_{\max}^{\rm EoS}\geq2\,M_\odot$. Here $\mathcal{M}_c=(m_1m_2)^{3/5}/(m_1+m_2)^{1/5}$, $q=m_2/m_1\leq1$, and $\Lambda_i=(2/3)k_{2,i}[R_i c^2/(Gm_i)]^5$. Broaden a fraction $\varepsilon=0.32$ of samples using a Fisher-estimated $\sigma_{\tilde{\Lambda}}(\tilde{\Lambda})$ for current detector sensitivity, with independent Gaussian broadening of width $\sigma_{\delta\tilde{\Lambda}}=500$. Tabulate the prior on a $128^4$ grid and compare simulated injections using IMRPhenomXAS_NRTidalv3, bilby, dynesty with 2048 live points, and relative binning. Compare direct inference with posterior reweighting, whose weights satisfy $w_i=\pi_{\rm target}(\vec\theta_i)/\pi_{\rm sampling}(\vec\theta_i)$.
assumptions: The qualitative induced-prior scaling assumes a weak mass dependence of neutron-star radius and a power-law Love number, $k_2\propto m^{-\alpha}$.
limits: Slightly asymmetric binaries can remain biased toward larger $\tilde{\Lambda}$ because of the $q=1$ boundary until the signal resolves the mass ratio sufficiently well.
Posterior reweighting redistributes existing samples and cannot generate samples in inadequately explored regions.

analysis.problem: How can photoionization-dependent line acceleration respond to a changing local radiation spectrum during radiation-hydrodynamic evolution without solving the photoionization problem in every cell at every timestep? analysis.method: XSTAR calculations provide training data for a 200-tree random forest that predicts infrared, optical, ultraviolet, and X-ray force multipliers from $(\xi,t,T_{\rm bb})$. Athena++ evaluates the surrogate during hydrodynamic evolution, with the local ultraviolet flux fraction used to select an equivalent blackbody temperature. The training grid contains 177,100 points spanning $-8\leq\log t\leq1$, $-2\leq\log\xi\leq5$, and $10^4\leq T_{\rm bb}/\mathrm{K}\leq10^6$, split 80%/20% for training/testing.

analysis.reason: The proposed circumbinary-disk route to neutron-star–core mergers is directly relevant to engine-driven fast optical transients and dense circumstellar environments. It provides useful population-level predictions, but the LFBOT association remains a proposed interpretation rather than a demonstrated transient-emission model.
analysis.result: Circumbinary-disk (CBD) interactions shrink progenitor orbits but also remove potential double neutron stars (DNSs) through premature neutron-star–core mergers. The fiducial DNS merger rate falls from approximately $23$ to $21\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, a reduction of $8\%$, reaching $28\%$ in the most strongly affected model. Premature mergers are proposed as LFBOT progenitors, with a fiducial rate $R_{\mathrm{LFBOT}}\simeq11\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$; approximately $87\%$ occur within the CBD lifetime, potentially retaining dense circumstellar material. DNS mergers with delays $\lesssim40\,\mathrm{Myr}$ decrease by $40\%$. Accretion raises the mean merging-DNS chirp mass by approximately $0.08M_\odot$, from approximately $1.20M_\odot$ to $1.28M_\odot$.
analysis.problem: How does bound gas retained after common-envelope evolution alter DNS formation, merger rates, delay times, and masses, and can the resulting premature neutron-star–core mergers supply an LFBOT channel? A related inference problem is that the overall DNS merger rate alone cannot distinguish the underlying binary-evolution physics.
analysis.method: The study couples COMPAS population synthesis to the spindler interpolation of hydrodynamic disk simulations, using 55 models with $10^7$ massive binaries each. Disk formation requires $j_{\mathrm{avail}}\geq j_{\mathrm{KEP}}$, where $M_{\mathrm{CBD}}=f_M M_{\mathrm{env}}$, $j_{\mathrm{avail}}=\beta J_{\mathrm{total}}/M_{\mathrm{env}}$, $\beta=f_J/f_M$, and $j_{\mathrm{KEP}}=\zeta\sqrt{G(M_1+M_2)R_{\mathrm{CBD,in}}}$, with $R_{\mathrm{CBD,in}}=2.5a_{\mathrm{post,CEE}}$ and $\zeta=4$. The fiducial parameters are $f_M=0.05$ and $\beta=3$. Orbital and mass evolution include super-Eddington accretion and wind angular-momentum loss. For an additional Galactic comparison sample, chirp masses are calculated from measured component masses and remaining inspiral times from current orbital parameters using the Peters equations.
limits: Potential X-ray visibility depends on accretion-flow geometry, beaming, and obscuration; accretion does not by itself establish an observable X-ray counterpart.

analysis.reason: This provides useful constraints on stellar mass loss and circumstellar-medium formation: proximity to the Eddington limit and local density inversions do not by themselves guarantee strong outflows. Its relevance is indirect rather than transient-specific, but the weak-wind predictions and their sensitivity to iron ionization are useful when evaluating progenitor mass-loss prescriptions.
analysis.result: The METUJE models predict weak AF-supergiant winds, typically $\dot{M}\sim10^{-10}$–$10^{-9}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, below observational estimates; proximity to the Eddington limit alone does not produce strong winds. Weak ultraviolet flux and the failure of Fe III to recombine to Fe II limit line driving, and differences in iron ionization are identified as the most likely explanation for discrepancies between mass-loss predictions. Extending the iron line list changes the calculated line force by less than 1%. Gray atmospheres develop density inversions at $T_{\rm eff}\lesssim8\,\mathrm{kK}$, whereas non-gray models substantially weaken them. The radial dispersion analysis finds no significant instability, while optically thick nonradial perturbations can be strongly unstable with $\omega\sim\sqrt{k}$. Hydrogen recombination does not drive the calculated winds, even where its available power can approach the wind kinetic power.
analysis.problem: Why do AF supergiants retain weak predicted line-driven winds despite approaching the Eddington limit and developing locally super-Eddington layers, and why do predicted mass-loss rates fall below observational estimates and earlier predictions? Related questions concern the stability of density inversions and whether missing line opacity or hydrogen recombination can supply additional driving.
analysis.method: The study combines spherical gray hydrostatic atmospheres, linear perturbation analysis with numerical solutions of the dispersion relation, and spherical stationary METUJE wind models coupling hydrodynamics, NLTE kinetic equilibrium, and comoving-frame radiative transfer. The gray models satisfy $\mathrm{d}p/\mathrm{d}r=\rho\kappa F/c-\rho GM/r^2$ and $\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}r=-3\kappa\rho F/(16\sigma T^3)$, with $F=\sigma T_{\rm eff}^4(R_*/r)^2$. The local Eddington factor is $\Gamma=\kappa\sigma T_{\rm eff}^4R_*^2/(cGM)$. A two-dimensional isothermal nonradial treatment gives $\omega^2=a^2(k_x^2+k_z^2)-i(|f_{x,\rho}|k_x+|f_{z,\rho}|k_z)$. Additional tests extend the iron line list and compare hydrogen recombination power with wind kinetic power.

key_highlights.title: The Goldilocks Prior: Physically Consistent Inference of Neutron Star Properties from Gravitational Wave Observations
key_highlights.result: In simulated binary-neutron-star signals, the Goldilocks prior reduces tidal-inference biases relative to the tested uniform and existing EoS-informed priors, including signals outside the adopted EoS ensemble.
